EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a very strong ring-breathing band at 993 cm⁻¹ with a companion near 1028 cm⁻¹, characteristic of para-disubstituted benzene. Candidate 4 (p-chlorobenzyl alcohol) is para-disubstituted and uniquely explains the 1028 cm⁻¹ band as a primary alcohol C–O stretch, whereas phenolic Ar–O stretches (candidates 5 or 9) would be expected near ~1240–1270 cm⁻¹, which is absent. The 802 cm⁻¹ band fits an aryl C–Cl/para-substituted ring out-of-plane feature, consistent with Cl in candidate 4. The weak 3423 cm⁻¹ band indicates an O–H stretch (GFQ-001), and the CH stretch region (2913/2997/3065 cm⁻¹) matches aromatic/aliphatic C–H (GFQ-003). The 1609 cm⁻¹ band is a typical aromatic C=C stretch and may be influenced by H-bonding (ENV-001). Overall, candidate 4 best matches the combination of para ring breathing, aryl Cl, and primary alcohol signatures.
